title: 2008 HMMT November General Round 1 Problem 4
statement: How many numbers between 1 and \(1,000,000\) are perfect squares but not perfect cubes?

solutions.text: \(9901000000=1000^{2}=10^{6}\). A number is both a perfect square and a perfect cube if and only if it is exactly a perfect sixth power. So, the answer is the number of perfect squares, minus the number of perfect sixth powers, which is \(1000-10=990\).
